groups.title: Count Good Nodes in Binary Tree

groups.title: Check If a Word Occurs As a Prefix of Any Word in a Sentence

groups.title: Design Browser History

groups.title: Minimum Number of Days to Make m Bouquets

groups.title: Find Critical and Pseudo-Critical Edges in Minimum Spanning Tree

groups.title: The kth Factor of n
groups.notes: Kth ascending positive divisor of N, -1 if too few; same factor-pair enumeration.

groups.title: Check If Array Pairs Are Divisible by k

groups.title: Max Value of Equation
groups.notes: Maximum yi+yj+|xi-xj| for distinct sorted-x points with x-distance<=K; same monotonic deque on y-x.

groups.title: Find Longest Awesome Substring
groups.notes: Both maximize the length of a contiguous substring whose characters can be rearranged into a palindrome. Both permit length 1e5; prefix parity masks and checking one-bit differences solve both alphabets.

geeksforgeeks:706292.notes: GFG uses lowercase letters; LC uses decimal digits. Use one parity bit per alphabet symbol.

groups.title: Number of Ways Where Square of Number Is Equal to Product of Two Numbers
groups.notes: Both count index triplets of both types: one array value squared equals the product of two distinct increasing-index elements in the other array. C360 lengths 100 versus LC 1000; frequency-based product counting handles both.

groups.title: Maximal Network Rank
groups.notes: Both maximize the number of undirected roads incident to a pair of distinct towns/cities, counting their shared road once. Both use at most 100 vertices; degree counts and an adjacency test solve both.

groups.title: Largest Substring Between Two Equal Characters
groups.notes: Both return the maximum number of characters strictly between equal characters, or -1 when no repeated character exists. Both use lowercase strings; storing first positions handles GFG length 1e5 and LC length 300.

groups.title: Sell Diminishing-Valued Colored Balls
groups.notes: Both sell a specified number of items from inventories of distinct types, each sale earning the current remaining count of its type, to maximize total revenue. Descending inventory batching solves both.

code360:12292.notes: C360 returns the exact total; its N<=1000 and inventory<=1000 imply total revenue <=500500000, below LC modulus 1000000007. LC applies that modulus for its larger bounds.

groups.title: Merge In Between Linked Lists
groups.notes: Both replace an inclusive interior interval X..Y/a..b of the first singly linked list with the entire second list and return the resulting head. Both use zero-based indices and exclude the endpoints; pointer splicing handles both including C360 length 1e6.

groups.title: Maximum Units on a Truck
groups.notes: Both choose boxes by type, given box count and units per box, subject to a truck capacity measured in boxes, maximizing total units. Both bound types and counts at 1000 and capacity at 1e6; descending units-per-box greedy solves both.

groups.title: Maximum Ascending Subarray Sum
groups.notes: Both maximize the sum of a strictly increasing contiguous subarray of positive integers. Linear run accumulation serves GFG n<=1e5 and LC n<=100.

groups.title: Count Pairs With XOR in a Range
groups.notes: Both count unordered index pairs i<j whose XOR lies in the inclusive interval LOW..HIGH. Both bound numbers and endpoints at 20000; binary-trie range counting handles C360 n<=10000 and LC n<=20000.

groups.title: Rotating the Box
groups.notes: Both rotate a box clockwise by 90 degrees and let # stones fall under gravity until supported by * obstacles, stones, or the bottom. Both preserve horizontal positions during rotation and begin with supported stones; the same rotation and row/column compaction handles dimensions 250 versus 500.

groups.title: Remove All Occurrences of a Substring
groups.notes: Both repeatedly remove the leftmost occurrence of a specified pattern, joining the remaining string, until none remain. Lowercase strings up to 1000 and the same output string contract are stated.

groups.title: Count Number of Special Subsequences
groups.notes: Both count index-distinct subsequences with positive runs of three ordered symbols, modulo 1000000007. Three running DP counters solve both in linear time; GFG bounds are unavailable.

geeksforgeeks:701873.notes: Map LC 0,1,2 to GFG a,b,c. Other lowercase letters permitted by GFG cannot participate and are ignored.

groups.title: Partition Array Into Two Arrays to Minimize Sum Difference
groups.notes: Both minimize the absolute sum difference while partitioning into equal-cardinality halves on even-length integer arrays. Cardinality-aware meet-in-the-middle handles LC length<=30; GFG numerical bounds are unavailable.

geeksforgeeks:710349.notes: GFG additionally permits odd lengths, requiring floor(n/2) and ceil(n/2) subset sizes. On even lengths the contracts coincide; the same cardinality-aware partition optimization extends to odd lengths.

groups.title: Minimum Bit Flips to Convert Number
groups.notes: Both return the number of differing binary bit positions between two nonnegative integers, equivalently the minimum individual bit flips to convert one to the other. Both bound inputs at 1e9; popcount of XOR solves both. Both minimize individual bit flips converting one integer to the other. C360 restricts inputs to 1..1e9 and LC permits zero; popcount of XOR handles both. The minimum individual bit flips between two integers equals the count of differing positions, popcount(start XOR goal). Both permit zero and at most31 significant bits.

groups.title: Number of Unique Subjects Taught by Each Teacher
groups.notes: Both group records by person and count distinct subject/project identifiers, ignoring department when deduplicating; the composite key is subject/project plus department. Output order is unrestricted and no numerical bounds are given.

groups.title: Amount of Time for Binary Tree to Be Infected
groups.notes: Both spread an effect from a supplied existing start node to adjacent binary-tree nodes in one minute per edge, returning the time until every node is reached. Both state unique nodes/values; BFS on parent-child adjacency solves LC 1e5, with C360 bounds unavailable.

groups.title: Minimize XOR
groups.notes: Both return x minimizing x XOR a/num1 subject to x having the same set-bit count as b/num2. Greedily preserving high set bits then adding low missing bits solves both; GFG bounds are unavailable.

groups.title: Find Right Interval
groups.notes: For every interval, return the index of the interval with smallest start>=its end, or-1. Unique starts remove ties; sorted starts and binary search O(NlogN) supports N1e4 and2e4.

groups.title: 4Sum II
groups.notes: Count indexed tuples choosing one element from each of four equal-length arrays whose sum is zero. Pair-sum counting O(N^2) supports Code360N500 and LCN200; repeated values count distinct indices on both.

groups.title: 132 Pattern
groups.notes: Renamed retrieval match: Check Array Pattern asks existence of i<j<k with A[i]<A[k]<A[j], exactly132-pattern boolean task. Monotone stack O(N) supports N1e5 and2e5 and same signed-value domain.

groups.title: Find Largest Value in Each Tree Row
groups.notes: Return largest node value on each binary-tree level. Same breadth-first level reduction; O(N) supports N1e3 and1e4, including empty trees. Initialize level maximum to negative infinity for LC signed values.

groups.title: Complement of Base 10 Integer
groups.notes: Both complement only the bits through the highest significant binary digit. A significant-bit mask XOR handles both bounds; LC1009 additionally permits zero, whose one-bit complement is one.

groups.title: Minimum Number of Operations to Make Array Empty
groups.notes: Both minimize rounds removing/completing two or three identical-valued items, with -1 for a singleton frequency. Frequency counting and ceil(count/3) handles length100000 for both.

groups.title: Find the Middle Index in Array
groups.notes: Both return the leftmost index whose strict left and strict right sums are equal, with zero outside an endpoint and -1 if absent. Prefix total and running left sum handle both signed-array bounds.

groups.title: Smallest Subtree with all the Deepest Nodes
groups.notes: The root of the smallest subtree containing all deepest nodes is exactly their lowest common ancestor. Both return that node; postorder depth/LCA tracking is linear for500/1000 nodes.

groups.title: Sum of Distances
groups.notes: Both return at each position the sum of absolute index gaps to every equal-valued position. Grouped prefix/suffix position sums give O(n) for both length100000 bounds.
